sources.title: README.md
sources.locator: Features; Background session persistence; Remote SSH repositories; CLI; Requirements; Technical stack
sources.finding: Native macOS terminal/worktree workspace uses libghostty and zmx daemon. CLI/deeplinks control worktrees/tabs/repos. Local and beta SSH repositories support persistence; remote zmx survives dropped SSH/laptop sleep. Presence badges, scripts and GitHub PR controls are documented.

sources.title: https://supacode.sh/
sources.locator: Built different; Buy once Use forever; Licensing questions
sources.finding: Marketing explicitly names Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode CLI agents. Basic costs USD 99 for one Mac, Standard USD 129 for two Macs; Team USD 79/seat minimum three. Lifetime app license includes one year of updates, optional USD 59 renewal for Basic/Standard. Trial permits five successful local worktree creations; SSH worktree creation remains free.

sources.title: LICENSE

sources.title: Supacode shipped application and execution paths
sources.locator: README Requirements, Building, terminal persistence and remote SSH sections; Workspace.swift; supacode-cli/Transport/Dispatcher.swift
sources.finding: The scoped product is a native macOS 26+ AppKit/SwiftUI application plus a macOS CLI that contacts it through a Unix socket. The distribution has no Windows/Linux, web, iOS or Android client. Agent terminals run locally or on user-owned SSH hosts.

sources.title: Supacode Pi and Grok integrations
sources.locator: AgentIntegrationFactory.swift lines 20-35; Models/SkillAgent.swift; PiExtensionContent.swift and GrokHookSettings.swift
sources.finding: The shipped integration factory explicitly implements Pi and Grok, with corresponding settings/extension installation and agent names. General terminals still allow arbitrary user-installed CLI agents.

sources.title: Supacode complete terminal launch branches
sources.locator: TerminalSurfaceRecipe.launch local/remote/bypass branches; Clients/Zmx, WorktreeTerminalManager and repository script settings inspected for Docker, Podman, VM and sandbox provisioning
sources.finding: The terminal launch factory either runs a command directly, attaches a local zmx session, or connects to a user SSH host with optional remote zmx persistence. The scoped app has no per-agent container/VM provisioning backend. Generic repository scripts can run user commands such as docker compose down; that is not a product sandbox mode.

sources.title: Supacode task and review architecture
sources.locator: WorktreeTaskStatus.swift; Features/Repositories, Features/FileExplorer and Clients/Repositories persistence; Resources/Skills/supacode-cli.md; supacode-cli command inventory searched for issue, task, coordinator, delegate, schedule, cron and diff
sources.finding: Task status is idle/running on a worktree; persistence stores repositories, terminal layouts and sidebar state rather than separate native issues. The supplied CLI skill controls panes/worktrees but defines no coordinator role. Commands and reducers have no autonomous schedule/event dispatch engine or native proposed-code diff viewer; Git diff counts and terminal tools are separate.

sources.title: Supacode local user data and access model
sources.locator: RepositoryPersistenceClient.swift; Models/TerminalLayoutSnapshot.swift; local socket transport and app models searched for human members, shared threads, roles, SAML and OIDC
sources.finding: The desktop app uses the current OS user's repository settings, terminal layout and local socket. It has no human-member workspace, shared prompting, organization role or SAML/OIDC login model. Commercial license seat assignment is a separate portal and does not create a shared desktop workspace.
